survey: A round wall/desk clock seen almost straight on (rim ellipse ratio 0.96, face ratio 0.95, both under 1% off a true ellipse, so they are round and match each other). Thick orange torus rim encloses a flat white face. The face has 12 navy hour bars (the 2 o'clock bar is hidden under the minute hand) and dot minute marks between them. The hour, minute and red second hands all pivot from one red centre cap; the second hand sits over the 7 o'clock bar, as hands sit above the face. The clock stands upright on the green shelf, touching it only at the bottom curve of the rim, with its contact shadow beneath. It has no feet, stand or flat base.

errors.where: bottom of the orange rim, where it meets the green shelf
errors.what: The clock stands upright on its round rim with no feet, stand or flat base. A round body resting on one curved point would roll or tip over, so as drawn it could not stand on the shelf.

fix: Give the round clock two small stubby feet or a short flat stand at the bottom of the orange rim, so it rests stably on the shelf. Keep the face, hands and rim unchanged.
